html:
The Blackfoot Confederacy, or Niitsítapi, is a union of related Algonquian-speaking peoples of the northern Great Plains: the Siksika, the Kainai (Blood) and the Northern and Southern Piikani (Peigan). Their lands ran from the North Saskatchewan River in Alberta south into Montana.

They were nomadic bison hunters on the shortgrass prairie. In the first half of the 1700s they got horses and guns, the guns through Cree and Assiniboine traders. With them they pushed the Shoshone and the Kutenai back into the mountains and became the strongest power of the northwest Plains. They fought the Crow and kept American trappers out of their land; in 1806 a party from the Lewis and Clark Expedition had a deadly clash with Piikani young men.

Smallpox, whisky traders and the end of the bison herds in the 1880s broke their way of life. Today three Blackfoot nations live in Alberta and the Blackfeet Nation in Montana.
